chief_complaint: intense flashback nightmares, hypervigilance, and severe avoidance behaviors 8 months after severe motor vehicle crash
hpi_details: 38M truck driver involved in a fatal multi-vehicle collision 8 months ago. Since the crash, has suffered nightly terrifying dreams re-experiencing the collision, waking up drenched in sweat with a pounding heart. Refuses to drive or sit in the front seat of any car, avoiding all highways. Exhibits extreme startle response to loud noises, emotional numbing, detachment from his wife, and feeling constantly on guard.
ideas: thinks he is losing his sanity because he cannot stop reliving the accident
concerns: terrified of hearing car horns or sirens when walking outside
expectations: wants medication to stop the nightmares so he can get restful sleep
social_hx: Former long-haul truck driver (currently on disability leave), non-smoker

clinical_knowledge.topic: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Chronic evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Chronic is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes trauma-focused psychotherapy, with medication selected for persistent symptoms and patient-specific risks.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: intense flashback nightmares, hypervigilance, and severe avoidance behaviors 8 months after severe motor vehicle crash

Key HPI features: 38M truck driver involved in a fatal multi-vehicle collision 8 months ago. Since the crash, has suffered nightly terrifying dreams re-experiencing the collision, waking up drenched in sweat with a pounding heart. Refuses to drive or sit in the front seat of any car, avoiding all highways. Exhibits extreme startle response to loud noises, emotional numbing, detachment from his wife, and feeling constantly on guard.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 86, BP 132/84. Patient appears tense and hypervigilant in clinic, scanning the room. Affect is constricted and anxious when discussing the accident. PCL-5 (PTSD Checklist) score 58/80 (high symptom burden). No psychotic symptoms or suicidal intent.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Chronic.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute suicidal or homicidal ideation.
management_principles: Psychotherapy (Gold Standard): refer to trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (TF-CBT), specifically Prolonged Exposure (PE) or Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR)
If medication is desired, select an SSRI or SNRI after evaluating comorbidity, interactions, and patient preference, with follow-up for benefit and adverse effects
For trauma-related nightmares, a clinician may consider prazosin only after reviewing blood pressure, concurrent antihypertensives, and orthostatic-fall risk
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 38M presenting with chronic symptom clusters of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (intrusive flashbacks/nightmares, avoidance of trauma cues, negative alterations in cognition/mood, and hyperarousal) lasting >8 months post-trauma.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 86, BP 132/84. Patient appears tense and hypervigilant in clinic, scanning the room. Affect is constricted and anxious when discussing the accident. PCL-5 (PTSD Checklist) score 58/80 (high symptom burden). No psychotic symptoms or suicidal intent.
reference_soap.plan: Refer for trauma-focused psychotherapy, such as prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, or EMDR, using shared decision-making. If medication is desired, select an SSRI or SNRI after reviewing comorbidity, interactions, and patient preference, with follow-up for benefit and adverse effects. For nightmares, a clinician may consider prazosin only after reviewing blood pressure, concurrent lisinopril, and orthostatic-fall risk. Avoid routine benzodiazepine use in PTSD. Reassess suicide and violence risk; arrange urgent emergency assessment if active intent, plan, or inability to remain safe emerges.

learning_objectives: Identify the four core diagnostic symptom clusters of DSM-5 PTSD (Intrusions, Avoidance, Negative Cognitions/Mood, Hyperarousal)
Understand why trauma-focused psychotherapies (Prolonged Exposure, EMDR, CPT) represent the primary evidence-based foundation of PTSD treatment
Select first-line SSRI/SNRI pharmacotherapy and utilize Prazosin specifically for trauma-related nightmares
Explain the neurobiological rationale why benzodiazepines are contraindicated in PTSD (interfering with amygdala/prefrontal fear extinction learning)

teaching.one_liner: Psychiatric evaluation for patient presenting with intense flashback nightmares, hypervigilance, and severe avoidance behaviors 8 months after severe motor vehicle crash.

must_ask.say: Can you tell me what happened during the crash, and when it occurred?
Do you have nightmares or flashbacks where you relive the accident?
Have you been avoiding driving, highways, or anything that reminds you of the crash?
Do you feel constantly on edge, startle easily, or have trouble sleeping?
Have you had thoughts of harming yourself or anyone else? If so, have you thought about a plan, access to means, or acting on it? How has this affected work and relationships?
